source_refs.note: Topic 18.3.1 and its genetic problem, answered (PDF 90-91); Figure 18.3 is replaced by the original diagram.

blocks.text: In incomplete dominance neither allele is fully dominant over the other, so the heterozygote shows a phenotype intermediate between those of the parents. In Japanese four-o'clock plants, red-flowered (RR) x white-flowered (WW) gives all heterozygous pink-flowered (RW) offspring, showing that neither the red allele R nor the white allele W is completely dominant.

blocks.alt: Four-o'clock flowers. Parents: a red flower (RR) crossed with a white flower (WW); gametes R, R and W, W; arrows lead to four pink F1 plants, genotypes RW, RW, RW, RW, phenotypes all pink. F1 x F1: two pink flowers; gametes R, W and R, W; arrows lead to four F2 plants: one red, two pink and one white.
blocks.caption: Figure 18.3: Incomplete dominance in Japanese 4-o'clock plants (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 18.3).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Parents, Red, White, Gametes, F1 plants, Genotypes RW (four), Phenotypes All Pink, F1 X F1, F2 plants, Genotypes RR, RW, RW, WW, Phenotypes 1: Red, 2: Pink, 1: White.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 18.3 gives all four F2 genotypes as RW. The F2 genotypes are RR (red), RW and RW (pink) and WW (white), as drawn above.
Crossing two pink plants (RW x RW) gives red (RR), pink (RW) and white (WW) in a 1:2:1 ratio.
